Saadia-specific moves preserved per data-source/saadia-gloss-table.json; Blau's notes (data-source/blau-genesis-notes.json) consulted for Bereshit 1-12.

translations.1: Then God spoke to Moses directly.
translations.2: This shall be the law of the one afflicted with leprosy, at the time of his purification — that report of him be brought to the imām.
translations.3: And the imām shall go out to outside the camp; and if he sees that the one afflicted with leprosy has recovered from the affliction of the leprosy, he shall ordain for him what is required.
translations.4: Then the imām shall give the order, and there shall be taken for the one being purified two clean sparrows, and a rod of cedar, and crimson silk, and hyssop.
translations.5: Then the imām shall give the order to slaughter one of them, in a clay vessel over water from a spring.
translations.6: And he shall take the living sparrow, and the cedar rod, and the crimson silk and the hyssop, and shall dip them — together with the living sparrow — in the blood of the slaughtered sparrow, over the water from a spring.
translations.7: And he shall sprinkle upon the one being purified from the leprosy seven times, and shall declare him pure; and he shall release the living sparrow upon the face of the wilderness.
translations.8: Then the one being purified shall wash his garments and shave off all his hair, and shall bathe in water and be pure; and after that he shall enter into the camp, and shall remain outside his dwelling for seven days.
translations.9: And on the seventh day he shall shave all the hair of his head and his beard and his eyebrows, together with the rest of his hair; and he shall wash his garments, and shall bathe his body in water and be pure.
translations.10: And on the eighth day he shall bring forward two sound rams, and one sound ewe-lamb in its first year, and three tenths of fine flour as an offering mixed with oil, and a log of oil.
translations.11: And the purifying imām shall station the purified man — and them — before God, at the entrance of the tent of the assembly.
translations.12: And the imām shall take one of the rams, to present it for the guilt-offering, along with the log of oil; and he shall wave them as a waving before God.
translations.13: Then he shall slaughter it in the place where the purification-offering and the ascending-offering are slaughtered — in the holy place — for the guilt-offering is like the purification-offering for the imām; it is among the choicest of the holy things.
translations.14: Then he shall take some of its blood and place it on the cartilage of the earlobe of the one being purified — the right one — and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the thumb of his right foot.
translations.15: And the imām shall take from the log of oil and pour it into his left palm.
translations.16: And he shall dip his right finger from the oil that is on his left hand, and shall sprinkle from it with his finger seven times before God.
translations.17: Then he shall place some of the remainder upon the cartilage of the earlobe of the one being purified — the right one — and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the thumb of his right foot, upon the blood of the guilt-offering.
translations.18: And what remains of it he shall place upon the head of the one being purified, and shall seek forgiveness for him before God.
translations.19: Then the imām shall perform the purification-offering, and shall seek forgiveness for the one being purified from his impurity; and after that he shall slaughter the ascending-offering.
translations.20: Then he shall cause the ascending-offering and the gift-offering to ascend upon the altar; and the imām shall seek forgiveness for him, and he shall be pure.
translations.21: And if he is poor, his hand not reaching to that, then let him bring one ram as the guilt-offering, for the waving, that forgiveness be sought for him; and one tenth of fine flour mixed with oil as a gift-offering, and a log of oil.
translations.22: And two turtle-doves or two young pigeons, according to what his hand can reach — one of them shall be a purification-offering, and the other an ascending-offering.
translations.23: He shall bring them, on the eighth day from the beginning of his purification, to the imām, to the entrance of the tent of the assembly, before God.
translations.24: And the imām shall take the ram of the guilt-offering and the log of oil, and the imām shall wave them as a waving before God.
translations.25: Then he shall slaughter it; and he shall take some of its blood and place it on the cartilage of the earlobe of the one being purified — the right one — and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the thumb of his right foot.
translations.26: And from the oil the imām shall pour into his left palm.
translations.27: And he shall sprinkle with his right finger from that oil which is on his left palm, seven times before God.
translations.28: Then he shall place from the oil that is in his palm upon the cartilage of the earlobe of the one being purified — the right one — and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the thumb of his right foot, upon the place of the blood of the guilt-offering.
translations.29: And the remainder of it he shall pour upon the head of the one being purified, and shall seek forgiveness for him before God.
translations.30: Then he shall perform one of the turtle-doves or of the young pigeons, according to what his hand can reach.
translations.31: According to what his hand can reach — one of them a purification-offering, and the other an ascending-offering, together with the gift-offering; and he shall seek forgiveness for him before God.
translations.32: This is the law for one who has had the affliction of leprosy, whose hand has not reached to that, at the time of his purification.
translations.33: Then God spoke to Moses and Aaron directly.
translations.34: When you enter the land of Canaan, which I am giving you as a possession, and I bring about an affliction of leprosy in some of the houses of the land of your possession —
translations.35: then the owner of the house shall come and inform the imām, saying: 'There has appeared to me in the house something resembling an affliction.'
translations.36: And the imām shall give the order, and they shall clear the house before he enters to inspect the affliction, so that nothing in it be made impure; and after that he shall enter and look upon it.
translations.37: And if he sees the affliction — behold, it is in the walls of the house as streaks of greenish or reddish hue, and their appearance is sunken in the wall —
translations.38: then let him go out from the house to its doorway, and quarantine it for seven days.
translations.39: Then he shall return on the seventh day; and if he sees that the affliction has spread in the walls of the house,
translations.40: he shall order that they remove the stones in which the affliction is, and they shall cast them outside the town into an impure place.
translations.41: And the house shall be scraped on the inside all around, and they shall cast the plaster which they have scraped outside the town into an impure place.
translations.42: And they shall take other stones, and bring them in place of those stones; and fresh plaster shall be taken and the house shall be re-plastered.
translations.43: And if the affliction returns and spreads in the house after the stones have been removed, and after the house has been scraped and re-plastered —
translations.44: then the imām shall enter and look; and behold, if the affliction has spread in the house, it is a consuming leprosy in the house — it is impure.
translations.45: And let him demolish it — its stones and its timber and all its plaster — and cast that outside the town into an impure place.
translations.46: And whoever enters the house throughout all the days during which it is in quarantine shall be impure until the evening.
translations.47: And whoever lies down in it shall wash his garments; and likewise everyone who eats in it shall wash his garments.
translations.48: And if the imām enters and looks, and behold the affliction has not spread in the house after the plastering, then let him declare it pure — for the affliction has healed.
translations.49: And he shall take for its purification-offering two sparrows, and a cedar rod, and crimson silk and hyssop.
translations.50: And he shall slaughter one of them in a clay vessel over water from a spring.
translations.51: And he shall take the cedar rod and the hyssop, and the crimson silk and the living sparrow, and shall dip them in the blood of the slaughtered sparrow and in the water from a spring, and shall sprinkle it upon the house seven times.
translations.52: And he shall declare it pure by means of the blood of the slaughtered sparrow, and the spring water, and the living sparrow, and the cedar rod, and the hyssop, and the crimson silk.
translations.53: And he shall release the living sparrow outside the town toward the face of the wilderness, and shall seek forgiveness for what is in the house, and it shall be pure.
translations.54: This is the law for all affliction of leprosy and of the scall,
translations.55: and the leprosy of garments and of houses,
translations.56: and the blemish and the spreading mark and the spot —
translations.57: to indicate the time of becoming impure and the time of purification. These are all the laws of leprosy.
